title: Essay: Mary and Christ across periods

cards.front: Byzantine Theotokos: describe the pose, figure style, drapery, and meaning.
cards.back:
Pose: Mary enthroned or standing, frontal, presenting the Christ Child
Figure style: Flat, elongated, hieratic (formal and otherworldly)
Drapery: Stylized linear folds, little sense of a body underneath
Formal elements: Gold background, no real space or depth
Meaning: Theotokos = "God-bearer"; Mary and Christ shown as divine and distant, the icon as a window to the holy

cards.front: Romanesque Throne of Wisdom (Morgan Madonna): describe the pose, figure style, drapery, and meaning.
cards.back:
Pose: Mary seated frontally; Christ upright on her lap, facing forward like a small adult
Figure style: Stiff, symmetrical, blocky
Drapery: Rigid, patterned, rhythmic folds
Formal elements: Painted wood, carved in the round, meant to be carried in processions
Meaning: Mary is the throne; Christ is divine wisdom

cards.front: French Gothic Queen of Heaven: describe the pose, figure style, drapery, and meaning.
cards.back:
Pose: Mary standing in an S-curve sway, holding the Child on her hip
Figure style: Elegant, courtly, slender, more human
Drapery: Deep, flowing, curving folds that show the body underneath
Formal elements: Crowned Mary; precious materials (Virgin of Jeanne d'Évreux: silver gilt and enamel)
Meaning: Mary as crowned Queen of Heaven, but also a mother; royal devotion and luxury

cards.front: Late Gothic tenderness and agony: describe the pose, figure style, drapery, and meaning.
cards.back:
Pose: Tenderness: the Child reaching playfully toward Mary's face. Agony: Mary holding the dead Christ across her lap (Röttgen Pietà)
Figure style: Expressive and emotional; in the Pietà, distorted and grotesque, emaciated Christ with exaggerated wounds
Drapery: Heavy, simplified folds that frame the emotion
Formal elements: Painted wood, small scale, for close personal viewing
Meaning: Invites the viewer to feel Mary's love or grief directly (private devotion, Andachtsbild)

cards.front: Essay thesis: how do images of Mary and Christ change from Byzantine to Late Gothic?
cards.back:
Distance: From divine and distant (Byzantine) to human and close (Late Gothic)
Pose: From frontal and enthroned to swaying, interacting, and finally grieving
Figure style: From flat and stiff to naturalistic, then expressive and distorted for emotion
Why: Devotion shifts from honoring God's majesty to feeling Mary's love and suffering personally
